Thanks for specifying the address, they are two separate ones indeed 🙂 

About monitoring the arrival of workers - I strongly advise not do conduct such activity and use the recordings for this purpose. The purposes of why cameras are used is the security of property, controlling access to premises, investigation of theft and damages. Monitoring employees (and taking further action based on this) is a whole other purpose which needs  legal basis + very transparent information to the employees. Legitimate interest is doubtful as such activity is quite unproportional and employers can take alternative means to evaluate their employees (including whether they stick to their working schedule). There have been several rulings/guidelines from Data Protection Authorities over Europe where such activity is deemed unlawful. E.g. the latest from [Ireland|https://www.irishlegal.com/articles/court-of-appeal-use-of-cctv-footage-to-investigate-employee-discipline-in-breach-of-data-protection-laws] “_The Court of Appeal has ruled that the use of CCTV security footage to investigate an employee discipline issue was unlawful because the footage was collected and processed for the specific purpose of security”._

As seen from the linked BA ticket CS tickets related to _I have an issue with my invoice_ come in from drivers usually in the beginning of the month - that’s because we are sending the emails to our drivers then & hence questions arise each month. The main question we’re trying to answer is those tickets related to us sending the invoice late. 

!Screenshot 2022-06-07 at 09.23.32.png|width=597,height=371!

So although we do see a jump in tickets related to the invoice in the beginning of the month only ~15% of them are related to drivers complaining about where’s my invoice (i.e. because we’re sending this out late). Hence previously estimated CS ticket impact of 500 EUR per month due to late invoices is incorrect. The CS ticket cost is ~75 EUR per month instead due to Bolt sending out the emails a few days late. 

Now which comes to the actual issues under this issue type we see a large portion of tickets related to drivers not understanding the difference between the driver app & driver portal (where they can find already issued invoices). These tickets contribute ~18% of all tickets. The main cause for these tickets is because the driver have actually received an email with the invoice & as the tax year was ending they will need all the invoices we’ve generated for the whole year. Hence the CS agents are just replying please find the historical invoices in your driver portal. I have no idea how the 2 sources are looking like & how easy it is to navigate between the 2 but I believe there’s room for improvement linking the provider portal with the driver app to make the navigation between the two more fluid. 

Next large chunk of tickets came from drivers who are not understanding the invoice ~14% of all tickets - these are mainly new drivers who are not understanding: 

# What even is this document & why do we issue this?
# Do I have to pay as the top row shows X amount but the row To Be Paid = 0
# To be paid = 0.02 EUR → do I have to make this transfer or can I just keep driving to pay this ‘debt’

I believe this can be fixed via comms when we’re onboarding the drivers to say that yes we are going to send you a monthly summary of your commission & the important row is the one where it says how much you need to pay etc. 

Also as I’ve analysed tickets from April 2022 there’s a lot of annual report/invoice requests ~8% of all tickets. The drivers want to see the yearly data in one document but currently it’s not possible & they will have to pull these from the driver portal for each month separately. I believe this has been discussed in billing previously but it would require large dev effort & the impact isn’t that large - they can use the monthly invoices instead. Another point to improve with comms to point drivers into driver portal & saying we’re not going to issue annual invoice.

But as expected there’s a lot of unrelated issues under this issue type. The topics can be seen below:

!Screenshot 2022-06-07 at 09.24.02.png|width=733,height=456!

So in general, not too many drivers are complaining about late invoices but we should improve the link between the app vs portal to make it crystal clear for the drivers. And when onboarding we should educate the drivers what’s the monthly invoice & where to find them

*Notes from the retro call:*

* There was no due date for the project (it was stop-start, took 6 months); this caused us to add related tasks and expand the scope. Identify pre-requisites needed from other teams (research part of the project). 
* Would have made more sense to start working on it once SOPs were in place
* Milestones were based on Food project, but turned out to be difficult to follow
* First versions of processes were lengthy (new topic, trying things out, less involvement from Safety) - test tool was very helpful (only added later on)
* No example of how to create HP content (we should have a framework)
* SOPs are created for an “ideal state”, we often have to reality check due to product maturity (eg. does the blocking matrix apply to Drive? a new one would have been better)
* Better collaboration between Drive OPS and Safety team (eg. mismatch between visions was discussed and figured out).

With CCTV used by drivers in their vehicles, we have taken a stance that drivers are the sole controllers for this activity. Meaning that they decide for what purposes and through what technical means they are going to process the data (i.e. being solely responsible for abiding to the data protection rules applicable). Bolt is here not a controller nor a processor, since we don’t instruct drivers to install the cameras, we don’t have access to the footage and we don’t have any decision power over the processing activity (e.g. means to ensure that CCTV installed follows the legal requirements). 

Taking this into account, I think we don’t want to provide drivers with exhaustive legal advice (which can be interpreted as us giving instructions for the processing activity) and rather have a help article with basic guidelines which basically state the following: 

_Bolt does not instruct and require the drivers to install CCTV in their vehicles and provide any video recordings to Bolt. However, if the driver would like to install CCTV, the following has to be taken in account._ 

_Driver is the controller of the personal data processed and has to ensure that there exists a legal basis for processing and comply with the applicable law and regulatory requirements. The requirements include, but are not limited to the following:_

* _Passengers are transparently notified about the CCTV in the vehicle (e.g. through a visible sign in the vehicle which informs about the fact of recording);_
* _Data subject rights (including objecting to the recording) must be ensured;_
* _Retention period is set for the storage period of the recordings;_
* _Appropriate technical and organisational measures must be implemented to ensure the security of the data._ 
* _Any disclosure of the recording must have a legal basis._

* Does not look like with existing labels per case we are able to provide reliable enough predictions on comment level for all required languages (i.e. we were similar on English, much better on Spanish, completely off for Russian and French - such instability in results refer to issues with our labels). * Decided to stop with ML based approach for now and look into labeling and reporting first. As an improvement in Q3 we can look into language based safety keyword routing - i.e. we don’t have an option to cross-check keyword for English comment if they were made in Germany, by estimating language of a comment first we can check with appropriate keyword set.

It is true that the law doesn't stipulate any requirements on in which form we check the driver’s license but rather that it has to be checked +each time before handing over a vehicle+. Therefore I don’t see any restrictions on accepting a photo copy of the driver’s license (the risk of counterfeits, recalls etc will however be on us if we choose to go this route). In regard to Swedish renters in particular, given that we have an up to date electronic register available as I understand, it will probably difficult for us to argue that we wasn’t aware of whether a drivers license was recalled or fake. I foresee that the result could be that if we receive a photo copy of a Swedish driver’s license and rely on that and it turns out that the driver’s license was fake or recalled,  we can be found to have acted negligent in regards to the applicable legislation. Much like intentional breaches of the applicable legislation, negligent breaches may also result in fines or jail up to six (6) months.

*

* An updated Insurance Certificate with any supporting documents, if relevant (such as the permission letter and/or policy schedule)

{code:sql}WITH stop_jitter AS (
  SELECT MIN(timestamp_ms) AS ts_start, MAX(timestamp_ms) AS ts_end, vehicle_id, order_id, ignition_id, gnss_pdop, gnss_hdop, lat, lng, ST_Point(lng, lat) AS pt
  FROM (
    SELECT *,
      SUM(igition_switch) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS ignition_id
    FROM (
      SELECT *, 
        COALESCE((
          (ignition != LAG(ignition) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms)) OR
          (order_id != LAG(order_id) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms))
        )::integer, 1) AS igition_switch
      FROM (
        SELECT timestamp_ms, entity_id AS vehicle_id, order_id, 
               JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'is_ignition_on') AS ignition,
               lat, lng,
               JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_pdop')::decimal AS gnss_pdop,
               JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_hdop')::decimal AS gnss_hdop
        FROM ext_tracking_live.tracking_car_sharing_locations
        WHERE created_at_date>'2022-05-01' AND JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_status')='fix' AND order_id!=0
          -- AND ST_DistanceSphere(ST_Point(lng,lat), ST_Point(24.745293, 59.437339)) < 15000 -- FILTER OUT FERRIES (hopefully), only 15km around Raekoja
          -- AND created_at_date='2022-05-14' AND order_id=3621305 -- EXTRA LIMIT TO REMOVE
          AND created_at_date='2022-05-24' -- AND created_at_date<'2022-06-04'--AND vehicle_id IN (1974,1254,777,1485,735,495,2013) -- EXTRA LIMIT TO REMOVE
      )
    )
  )
  WHERE ignition='false'
  GROUP BY vehicle_id, order_id, ignition_id, gnss_pdop, gnss_hdop, lat, lng
),



stop_centroid AS (
  SELECT vehicle_id, order_id, ignition_id,
    ST_Centroid(ST_Collect(pt)) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY lat,lng) AS centroid-- ,
    -- ST_Area(ST_ConvexHull(ST_Collect(l.pt))::geography) AS area_m2,
    -- ST_Perimeter(ST_ConvexHull(ST_Collect(l.pt))::geography) AS perimeter_m
  FROM stop_jitter
  WHERE gnss_pdop = 0 AND gnss_hdop = 0
  GROUP BY 1,2,3
  HAVING COUNT(1) >= 3 -- at least SOME jitterin to filter out least accurate centroids
),


stop_accuracy AS (
  SELECT j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id, 
    -- MIN(ts_start) AS ts_start,
    -- MAX(ts_end) AS ts_end,
    MAX(ST_DistanceSphere(j.pt, centroid)) AS accuracy_m --,
    -- ANY_VALUE(SQRT(area_m2)) AS area_sqrt_m,
    -- ROUND(accuracy_m/NULLIF(area_sqrt_m, 0)) AS ratio
  FROM stop_jitter AS j
  JOIN stop_centroid AS c ON (j.vehicle_id = c.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = c.order_id AND j.ignition_id = c.ignition_id)
  WHERE j.gnss_pdop = 0 AND j.gnss_hdop = 0
  GROUP BY j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id
  HAVING accuracy_m < 300 -- TOWING and FERRIES are above that threshold, based on a few days sampling (>2022-05-24 & <2022-06-04)
),



stop_dillution AS (
   SELECT d0.vehicle_id, d0.order_id, d0.ignition_id,
          CEIL(MAX(ST_DistanceSphere(j.pt, centroid))) AS worst_accuracy_m,
          MAX(gnss_hdop) AS max_gnss_hdop,
          MAX(gnss_pdop) AS max_gnss_pdop,
          COUNT(1) AS ignition_hits
   FROM stop_accuracy AS d0
   JOIN stop_centroid AS c ON (c.vehicle_id = d0.vehicle_id AND c.order_id = d0.order_id AND c.ignition_id = d0.ignition_id)
   JOIN stop_jitter AS j ON (j.vehicle_id = d0.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = d0.order_id AND j.ignition_id = d0.ignition_id)
   GROUP BY 1,2,3
   HAVING worst_accuracy_m < 400
),



stop_accuracy_per_ignition AS (
  SELECT j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id, j.gnss_pdop, j.gnss_hdop,
         MAX(ST_DistanceSphere(j.pt, centroid)) AS worst_accuracy_m,
         COUNT(1) AS hits
  FROM stop_jitter AS j
  JOIN stop_centroid AS c ON (j.vehicle_id = c.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = c.order_id AND j.ignition_id = c.ignition_id) -- SKIPPING ignition_ids without the 0,0 accuracy
  JOIN stop_dillution AS d ON (j.vehicle_id = d.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = d.order_id AND j.ignition_id = d.ignition_id) -- AND filtering out the towing & location updates reorder
  GROUP BY j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id, j.gnss_pdop, j.gnss_hdop, ST_AsEWKT(centroid)
),



stop_median AS (
  SELECT gnss_hdop, gnss_pdop,
        MEDIAN(worst_accuracy_m) AS median_worst_accuracy_m,
        SUM(hits) AS hits
  FROM stop_accuracy_per_ignition
  GROUP BY gnss_hdop, gnss_pdop
),



stop_thresholds AS (
  SELECT hi.gnss_hdop, hi.gnss_pdop,
    -- ANY_VALUE(hi.median_worst_accuracy_m) AS old_median_worst_accuracy_m,
    MAX(lo.median_worst_accuracy_m) AS median_worst_accuracy_m,
    ANY_VALUE(hi.hits) AS hits
  FROM stop_median AS hi
  JOIN stop_median AS lo ON (hi.gnss_hdop >= lo.gnss_hdop AND hi.gnss_pdop >= lo.gnss_pdop)
  WHERE hi.hits > 9
  GROUP BY 1,2
)


SELECT a.gnss_hdop, a.gnss_pdop,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p50,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p75,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p95,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.97) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p97,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p99,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.995) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p995,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.999) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p999,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.9999) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p9999,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.99999) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p99999,
  SUM(hits) AS hits
FROM stop_accuracy_per_ignition AS a
JOIN stop_thresholds AS t ON (a.gnss_hdop = t.gnss_hdop AND a.gnss_pdop = t.gnss_pdop)
WHERE worst_accuracy_m >= median_worst_accuracy_m
GROUP BY gnss_hdop, gnss_pdop
ORDER BY 1,2
LIMIT 300
{code}

+Fines:+

 

The Slovak Protection Act sets out a fine in the amount of EUR 66,400 for each case of breach of the legislation. The fine is imposed by the Customer Protection Agency (the “*Agency*”) and is payable by the relevant business whose products are discounted. The fine can be imposed p. e. in cases when the Agency considers the campaign as misleading in terms of distinguity of discounted products, the amount of the discount, or if the products are sold at the discounted price for a very long time.

 

If the customer protection regulation is breached by the business in more than one case (p. e. more than one campaign is non-compliant), the amount of the fine rises up to EUR 166,000 for each case of the breach. On the other hand, if the Agency considers the breach as not too serious and easily fixable, it may ask the business to change the campaign accordingly, without imposing a fine.

+Criminal liability:+

In borderline cases, if a campaign is extremely non-compliant and is effectively able to cause damages to a broad range of customers, or if the campaign improperly and negatively affects other businesses, criminal sanctions might be imposed at the business and its management body. Criminal sanctions vary and may include imposing a fine, a ban on performance of business activities, or and imprisonment. In this case, Bolt might also be criminally liable for such conduct, as a so called _helper_.

Please note that usually, the criminal liability takes place in cases of a very serious breach of the customer protection regulation and mostly requires an intentional conduct of the business/Bolt (as helper) to cause damages to a customer. In most cases, less serious breaches are fixable at proceedings before the Agency as mentioned above.

1.3.   Materjali andmisega Töövõtja kasutusse ei kaasne ühegi Tellijale kuuluva litsentsi või Tellija IOÕ üleminekut Töövõtjale. 1.5.   Töövõtja annab Tellijale ainulitsentsi käesolevas peatükis nimetatud intellektuaalse omandiga seotud autori isiklike õiguste kasutamiseks ilma geograafiliste piiranguteta kogu selliste õiguste kehtivuse ajaks vastavalt seadusele.

Further relevant suggestions from Gatsby guys:


* you use both {{createPages}} & {{onCreatePage}}— this is bad because you're doubling (at least) the work to create each page. Just do whatever calculations you need up front to create the right pages & set the context. 
*We need to pass extra context to each page so we might still need it.* 
* move the creation of redirects to onPostBootstrap — you're recreating redirects on every incremental build
*Not tested yet. but commented out since we don’t need redirects for a production build. But this did not decrease the build time.*
* the .htaccess stuff isn't needed on Gatsby Cloud
*this is not used and we can remove it.*
* One other thing I noticed — you're querying a lot of fields in createPages that you don't use for creating the pages — e.g. city.description.description. Queries get slower to run the more fields you add (generally speaking). You can measure how long the query takes to run before and after removing unnecessary fields.
*We need to investigate that too but a win here won't be significant since we use most of the fields that we are querying*
* Gatsby has native ts support now for gatsby-node\! [https://github.com/gatsbyjs/gatsby/discussions/34613|https://github.com/gatsbyjs/gatsby/discussions/34613|smart-link]  — we've seen people get a lot of memory back switching to this

When a user is logged out of their Bolt account for a set amount of time, the account will be automatically archived in case there is an attempt to log in with the same phone number on a different device (or the same device after a system update).

The period after which an account can be auto-archived depends on the area code of the phone number associated with the account. Those timeframes are:

* Global: 180 days
* Estonia: 60 days
* Nigeria and Kenya: 90 days
* Slovakia: 720 days.

This is covered in 🚗🥡 *Rider or eater requests to delete account* 💫

{code:sql}WITH stop_jitter AS (
    SELECT MIN(timestamp_ms) AS ts_start, MAX(timestamp_ms) AS ts_end, vehicle_id, order_id, ignition_id, gnss_pdop, gnss_hdop, lat, lng, ST_Point(lng, lat) AS pt
    FROM (
             SELECT *,
                    SUM(igition_switch) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS ignition_id
             FROM (
                      SELECT *,
                             COALESCE((
                                              (ignition != LAG(ignition) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms)) OR
                                              (order_id != LAG(order_id) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms))
                                          )::integer, 1) AS igition_switch
                      FROM (
                               SELECT timestamp_ms, entity_id AS vehicle_id, order_id,
                                      JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'is_ignition_on') AS ignition,
                                      lat, lng,
                                      JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_pdop')::decimal AS gnss_pdop,
                                      JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_hdop')::decimal AS gnss_hdop
                               FROM ext_tracking_live.tracking_car_sharing_locations
                               WHERE created_at_date>'2022-05-20' AND JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_status')='fix' AND order_id!=0
                               -- AND ST_DistanceSphere(ST_Point(lng,lat), ST_Point(24.745293, 59.437339)) < 15000 -- FILTER OUT FERRIES (hopefully), only 15km around Raekoja
                               -- AND created_at_date='2022-05-14' AND order_id=3621305 -- EXTRA LIMIT TO REMOVE
                               -- AND created_at_date='2022-05-24' -- AND created_at_date<'2022-06-04'--AND vehicle_id IN (1974,1254,777,1485,735,495,2013) -- EXTRA LIMIT TO REMOVE
                           ) AS field_extract
                  ) AS ignition_switch
         ) AS ignition_id
    WHERE ignition='false'
    GROUP BY vehicle_id, order_id, ignition_id, gnss_pdop, gnss_hdop, lat, lng
),



stop_centroid AS (
 SELECT vehicle_id, order_id, ignition_id,
        ST_Centroid(ST_Collect(pt)) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY lat,lng) AS centroid-- ,
        -- ST_Area(ST_ConvexHull(ST_Collect(l.pt))::geography) AS area_m2,
        -- ST_Perimeter(ST_ConvexHull(ST_Collect(l.pt))::geography) AS perimeter_m
 FROM stop_jitter
 WHERE gnss_pdop = 0 AND gnss_hdop = 0
 GROUP BY 1,2,3
 HAVING COUNT(1) >= 3 -- at least SOME jitterin to filter out least accurate centroids
),


stop_accuracy AS (
 SELECT j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id,
        -- MIN(ts_start) AS ts_start,
        -- MAX(ts_end) AS ts_end,
        MAX(ST_DistanceSphere(j.pt, centroid)) AS accuracy_m --,
        -- ANY_VALUE(SQRT(area_m2)) AS area_sqrt_m,
        -- ROUND(accuracy_m/NULLIF(area_sqrt_m, 0)) AS ratio
 FROM stop_jitter AS j
  JOIN stop_centroid AS c ON (j.vehicle_id = c.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = c.order_id AND j.ignition_id = c.ignition_id)
 WHERE j.gnss_pdop = 0 AND j.gnss_hdop = 0
 GROUP BY j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id
 HAVING accuracy_m < 300 -- TOWING and FERRIES are above that threshold, based on a few days sampling (>2022-05-24 & <2022-06-04)
),



stop_dillution AS (
 SELECT d0.vehicle_id, d0.order_id, d0.ignition_id,
        CEIL(MAX(ST_DistanceSphere(j.pt, centroid))) AS worst_accuracy_m,
        MAX(gnss_hdop) AS max_gnss_hdop,
        MAX(gnss_pdop) AS max_gnss_pdop,
        COUNT(1) AS ignition_hits
 FROM stop_accuracy AS d0
  JOIN stop_centroid AS c ON (c.vehicle_id = d0.vehicle_id AND c.order_id = d0.order_id AND c.ignition_id = d0.ignition_id)
  JOIN stop_jitter AS j ON (j.vehicle_id = d0.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = d0.order_id AND j.ignition_id = d0.ignition_id)
 GROUP BY 1,2,3
 HAVING worst_accuracy_m < 400
),



stop_accuracy_per_ignition AS (
 SELECT j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id, j.gnss_pdop, j.gnss_hdop,
        MAX(ST_DistanceSphere(j.pt, centroid)) AS worst_accuracy_m,
        COUNT(1) AS hits
 FROM stop_jitter AS j
  JOIN stop_centroid AS c ON (j.vehicle_id = c.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = c.order_id AND j.ignition_id = c.ignition_id) -- SKIPPING ignition_ids without the 0,0 accuracy
  JOIN stop_dillution AS d ON (j.vehicle_id = d.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = d.order_id AND j.ignition_id = d.ignition_id) -- AND filtering out the towing & location updates reorder
 GROUP BY j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id, j.gnss_pdop, j.gnss_hdop, ST_AsEWKT(centroid)
),



stop_median AS (
 SELECT gnss_hdop, gnss_pdop,
        MEDIAN(worst_accuracy_m) AS median_worst_accuracy_m,
        SUM(hits) AS hits
 FROM stop_accuracy_per_ignition
 GROUP BY gnss_hdop, gnss_pdop
),



stop_thresholds AS (
 SELECT hi.gnss_hdop, hi.gnss_pdop,
        -- ANY_VALUE(hi.median_worst_accuracy_m) AS old_median_worst_accuracy_m,
        MAX(lo.median_worst_accuracy_m) AS median_worst_accuracy_m,
        ANY_VALUE(hi.hits) AS hits
 FROM stop_median AS hi
          JOIN stop_median AS lo ON (hi.gnss_hdop >= lo.gnss_hdop AND hi.gnss_pdop >= lo.gnss_pdop)
 WHERE hi.hits > 9
 GROUP BY 1,2
)




SELECT a.gnss_hdop, a.gnss_pdop,
       ANY_VALUE(median_worst_accuracy_m) AS median_worst_accuracy_m,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p50,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p75,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p95,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.97) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p97,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p99,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.995) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p995,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.999) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p999,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.9999) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p9999,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.99999) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY worst_accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p99999,
       COUNT(1) AS rows,
       SUM(a.hits) AS taken_hits,
       SUM(t.hits) AS original_hits
FROM stop_accuracy_per_ignition AS a
JOIN stop_thresholds AS t ON (a.gnss_hdop = t.gnss_hdop AND a.gnss_pdop = t.gnss_pdop)
WHERE worst_accuracy_m >= median_worst_accuracy_m/3
GROUP BY a.gnss_hdop, a.gnss_pdop
ORDER BY 1,2
LIMIT 300
{code}

*Location logic:*

* We have 2 ways of getting location from OS - {{requestLocationUpdates}} (system emits updated location to our callback) and {{getLastLocation}} (we ask system to provide last known location)
* Some code relies on first method (to receive and handle updates), and some code relies on second method (to just get latest location and do something with it)

*What happened to user according to logs:*

* On first app open, only 1 location was emitted from {{requestLocationUpdates}} and there were no more updates from the system. However, {{getLastLocation}} was called multiple times after that, returning updated location each time.
* App was in background for several hours, but the process was not killed
* On next app open, carsharing screen used cached location from {{requestLocationUpdates}} (which was received several hours ago) and moved the map to wrong location. Other places in code used {{getLastLocation}} and received correct location, so blue dot on map had correct position.

*Possible reasons of error:*

* Something is wrong with our rx chain for {{requestLocationUpdates}} method, maybe it receives error or terminate event at some point and don’t emit any new values
* Something is wrong with OS location services/sdk and the system doesn’t emit new location to our callback, which is passed to {{requestLocationUpdates}}

*Taken steps:*

* Added logs to {{requestLocationUpdates}} rx chain to later investigate if it’s problem with the chain
* Used {{getLastLocation}} in carsharing map movement logic, because we don’t rely on location updates in that part and all we need is to get latest location. This will fix this exact issue, but will not fix the root cause, still need to investigate {{requestLocationUpdates}} flow.

In an effort to understand if “very fast delivery” is an important value prop for Bolt Market, we want to run some experiments. The experiments will include artificially increasing the ETA that is shown to users on the home screen and the menu screen, so that we would see how it impacts conversion to checkout and orders.
The experiment will affect the following 4 stores in Riga:


* 30107 - Bolt Market Bieziņa
* 32878 - Bolt Market Daugavgrīvas
* 36217 - Bolt Market Spulgas
* 40250 - Bolt Market Liepājas

We will target users randomly, and users will fall into one of the following three cohorts:


* Control group (34% of users): no changes in the ETA
* Treatment group 1 (33% of users): the ETA that will be shown will be 10 minutes higher than what we calculated
* Treatment group 2 (33% of users): the ETA that will be shown will be 15 minutes higher than what we calculated

*The test will start on Monday (13.06.2022) and will last for 2 weeks.*
We will create dashboards next week to check the behaviour of each of the user groups, but in the meantime you can check the orders per store and conversion rates per store to understand the impact of the experiment. If you have any questions/concerns, please take them up in this thread.

Hi Getter,

Closing down some of the backlog items and I reached to this one.

For absence, Workday has two separate approaches: time off and leave of absence:

# *Time off*: this is the standard approach for annual leave; it comes with a plan and a balance (or just an open balance without limit). It is normally used for annual leave entitlements but it can be configured for all sorts of absence, in general short term. You book units in your calendar, be it hours or days, medical visits, short term sickness, maybe jury duty might fall under this type. Workers do not appear “On Leave” in Workday when they book time off and there is no return to work process associated with these requests. 
# *Leave of Absence*: this is the standard approach for long term leaves; be it maternity, paternity, parental leave or long term sickness. Compared to time off, you do not have a balance but rather eligibility rules. When the leave starts, workers will show up as “On Leave” in Workday and the request; when you request it you input an estimated last day of leave and workers need to initiate return to leave process to input the actual last day of leave.

This is the general approach, but from country to country the set-up can differ, based on the benefits provided and legal requirements. It is common to see sick leave as both time off and leave of absence depending on the period (short vs long term). 

When it comes to reporting, time off and leave of absence are reported separately. We cannot combine both time off and leave of absence in one single report because of the different characteristics. This is the reason why Fabian’s parental leave did not show in “All worker time off” but in the “Workers on leave” report. For Payroll extracts/integrations, the approach is different.

So in order to get the data that you need, one needs to know the different eligible time off plans and leave of absence type for the eligible population. If this is not clear we can definitely help with explaining the available options.

Kind regards,

Olivian

{noformat}with summary as (select 
	date_part(week, dir.created) as week,
	date_part(year, dir.created) as year,
	dpp.vendor_id as vendor_id,
	from_agent_id as provider_id,
	coalesce(sum(case when dir.type = 'fee' then sum_with_vat end),0) as fee_sum_loc,
	coalesce(sum(case when dir.type = 'fee' then sum_with_vat/vw.rate end),0) as fee_sum_eur,
	null as adjustment_sum_loc,
	null as adjustment_sum_eur,
	coalesce(sum(case when dir.type in ('payout') then sum_with_vat end),0) as payout_sum_loc,
	coalesce(sum(case when dir.type in ('payout') then sum_with_vat/vw.rate end),0) as payout_sum_eur
	from delivery.delivery_invoicing_record dir 
	left join delivery.delivery_provider_provider dpp on dpp.id = dir.from_agent_id 
	left join vw_currency_exchange_rates vw on vw.valid_on = DATE(dir.created) and vw.currency = dir.currency 
	where dir.created >= '2020-12-28' and dir.created < '2022-01-03'
	and dir.from_agent_id in (13309,20804,20807,20809,20810,20812,34338)
	and dir.from_agent_type = 'delivery_provider'
	group by 1,2,3,4
union 
select 
	date_part(week, dir.created) as week,
	date_part(year, dir.created) as year,
	dpp2.vendor_id as vendor_id,
	to_agent_id as provider_id,
	null as fee_sum_loc,
	null as fee_sum_eur,
	coalesce(abs(sum(case when dir.type = 'adjustment' then sum_with_vat end)),0) as adjustment_sum_loc,
	coalesce(abs(sum(case when dir.type = 'adjustment' then sum_with_vat/vw.rate end)),0) as adjustment_sum_eur,
	coalesce(sum(case when dir.type = 'payoutReject' then -sum_with_vat end),0) as payout_sum_loc,
	coalesce(sum(case when dir.type = 'payoutReject' then -sum_with_vat/vw.rate end),0) as payout_sum_eur
	from delivery.delivery_invoicing_record dir 
	left join delivery.delivery_provider_provider dpp2 on dpp2.id = dir.to_agent_id 
	left join vw_currency_exchange_rates vw on vw.valid_on = DATE(dir.created) and vw.currency = dir.currency 
	where dir.created >= '2020-12-28' and dir.created < '2022-01-03'
	and dir.to_agent_id in (13309,20804,20807,20809,20810,20812,34338)
	and dir.to_agent_type = 'delivery_provider'
	group by 1,2,3,4
) select 
coalesce(week, 0) as week,
coalesce(year, 0) as year,
coalesce(vendor_id, 0) as vendor_id,
coalesce(provider_id, 0) as provider_id,
sum(coalesce(fee_sum_loc,0)) + sum(coalesce(adjustment_sum_loc,0)) as invoiced_sum_loc,
round(sum(coalesce(fee_sum_eur,0)) + sum(coalesce(adjustment_sum_eur,0)),2) as invoiced_sum_eur,
sum(coalesce(payout_sum_loc,0)) as payout_sum_loc,
round(sum(coalesce(payout_sum_eur,0)),2) as payout_sum_eur
from summary
group by 1,2,3,4
order by 1 asc{noformat}

Further information as per discussion with OC and then [~accountid:61f105a058ce4f00688c83f9] and [~accountid:5b76bc2cb974540708ee16ee] : 

* +Sur la nécessité d’utiliser un support durable:+
** La DGCCRF estime qu’un sms n’est pas archivable et qu’il n’est pas possible d’y ajouter une PJ, dès lors elle en fait une interprétation qui ne l’inclut pas dans la catégorie des supports durables. La doctrine sur ce point est en outre très claire. 
** Cependant, le risque encouru paraît limité → contrôle de la DGCCRF et amande administrative. Le risque pénal mentionné dans le Mémo d’OC relève plus de pratiques commerciales sanctionnables, telles que pratique trompeuse si on ne donne pas le prix etc. 
** Une solution serait d’envisager que l’agent qui prend la communication crée un compte au nom et pour le compte du client, compte dans lequel toutes les factures seraient mises en ligne → support durable (/)  On pourrait envisager une création de compte par l’agent avec un mot de passe standard et la possibilité de le changer à la 1ère connexion. 
* +Sur les informations à donner au téléphone:+ 
** Il est suffisant de communiquer le prix estimé
** Idéalement il faudrait aussi mentionner que le prix peut varier en fonction de facteurs externes tels que la circulation et de la météo (comme cela est précisé dans l’App). 
** Il faut mentionner que le prix définitif sera confirmé en fin de course.
* Sur le fait d’obtenir ou non l’acceptation des T&Cs par le nouveau client:
** Si l’on n’obtient par leur consentement, le risque est qu’on ne puisse pas leur opposer les T&Cs - par exemple la clause qui dit qu’ils doivent rembourser le nettoyage de la voiture en cas de problème… 
** Un premier step serait de mettre le lien des T&Cs dans un sms et de le mentionner au téléphone

* +Sur les informations à communiquer par sms:+
** Donner l’estimation du temps de trajet et l’ETA + l’estimation du prix
** Mettre le lien des T&Cs en PDF
** *1st sms:*
*** _Please download our T&Cs for your records \[here]. You car model X license plate X driven by NAME should arrive at location PLACE at ETA. Your destination is X. The price estimate of this ride is X. Here is the link to the webpage with all the pricing parameters per city._ 
*** _Veuillez télécharger nos CGV pour vos archives. Votre voiture, modèle X, plaque d'immatriculation X, conduite par NOM, devrait arriver au lieu LIEU à ETA Xh. Votre destination est X. Le prix estimé de cette course est X. Voici le lien vers la page web avec tous les paramètres de tarification par ville._
** *2nd sms:*
*** _Please download the invoice for your records \[here]._
*** _Veuillez télécharger la facture pour vos archives._ 
* +Autres:+
** Penser à demander à *l’agent de suivre la course à distance pour pouvoir informer le client en cas de changement* de chauffeur, annulation, retard conséquent, etc 
** *Donner la possibilité au client d’annuler la course si changement substantiel de l’ETA*.

Main ideas:
1) It would be good to have overall estimation of the test (which incrmntal does not do).

2) Also we cannot statistically speak about the exact number of incremental installs.

3) Using Binomial distribution might be good. But we also have to be careful here since the days are not independent. (e.g. if the model fails to predict one day, it has more probability to fail the other one).

The criterion of having the actual *line beyond* the prediction *over more than 3 days* might be a solution. But we should take to consideration:But we should take to consideration:

* there still might be confounders
* there are peaks connected to something else


An indicator of a confounder might be that we have only two days beyond the interval and they do come in a row.

To prevent failover due to max connection or max task limit, we need to collect more data from the MySQL master

* Error message

MySQL will give away the following multiple messages to the log file and journalctl if it reached to max connection or max task limit

{noformat}2022-06-08T23:34:53.905784Z 0 [Warning] Too many connections
2022-06-08T23:34:53.906215Z 0 [Warning] Too many connections{noformat}

* Numbers of running processes.

max_connections=2000

Currently running user process = 613

taskLimit = 10000

{noformat}sangsun@target-d3:~$ cat /etc/mysql/my.cnf | grep max_connection
max_connections=2000
sangsun@target-d3:~$ sudo systemctl status mysql | grep Tasks
    Tasks: 613 (limit: 10000)
{noformat}

* Socket file existence

There are differences in socket files if MySQL is actually down

{noformat}root@target-d3-old:/home/sangsun# ls -al /var/run/mysqld/
total 0
drwxr-xr-x  2 mysql mysql  40 Jun  8 23:46 .
drwxr-xr-x 23 root  root  900 Jun 10 12:40 ..
{noformat}



{noformat}sangsun@target-d3:~$ ls -al /var/run/mysqld/
total 8
drwxr-xr-x  2 mysql mysql 100 Jun  9 08:53 .
drwxr-xr-x 23 root  root  900 Jun 10 12:34 ..
-rw-r-----  1 mysql mysql   6 Jun  9 08:53 mysqld.pid
srwxrwxrwx  1 mysql mysql   0 Jun  9 08:53 mysqld.sock
-rw-------  1 mysql mysql   6 Jun  9 08:53 mysqld.sock.lock{noformat}

* Check on listening port

{noformat}sangsun@target-d3:~$ sudo netstat -tnlp | grep 3306
tcp        0      0 0.0.0.0:3306            0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN      25268/mysqld {noformat}

Bolt Balance uses the currency of the country where the user is located.
If a user has a positive balance in one currency and travels to a country that uses a different currency, their Bolt Balance in that currency is saved and will be available as soon as the user returns.
Until the user returns to a country matching the currency of their balance, their Bolt Balance won't be visible in the app. For example, if a user has a positive balance in Euros they will only be able to view their balance when they are in a country that uses this currency.
Due to regulations and not supporting currency conversion in the app, it is not possible to transfer a user's balance from one currency to another.

{noformat}WITH clevertap_campaign_properties AS (
        
  SELECT
    channel
    ,conversion_event
    ,delivery
    ,device
    ,labels
    ,last_update
    ,message_id
    ,message_name
    ,start_date
    -- Every time the campaign is started or stopped, a new row is added - we only want to keep the latest row for each campaign
    ,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY message_id ORDER BY start_date desc) AS row_nr
    ,MIN(start_date) OVER(PARTITION BY message_id) AS first_start_dt
  FROM public.converted_clevertap_driver_campaign_properties
)

-- The journeys contain message and segmentation nodes, the manually collected data only contains message nodes
-- This subquery cleans up the segmentation node gaps in the node order nrs
,node_order_number AS (

  SELECT *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY journey_id ORDER BY node_id) AS node_order_number
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT journey_id, node_id
    FROM google_sheets_marketing.lifecycle_journeys
    WHERE lower(domain) = 'driver')
  ORDER BY 1, 2
)

,clevertap_journey_message_properties AS (

  SELECT DISTINCT
    j.journey_id,
    j.journey_name,
    j.campaign_id,
    j.goal_1_name,
    j.goal_2_name,
    j.goal_3_name,
    j.channel,
    j.campaign_name,
    j.node_id,
    -- There can be multiple message IDs per one journey message nodes (for example if there are different language variants)
    -- All these message IDs have the same content, so we want to aggregate to message node level in the reports
    -- Creating a field which keep one message ID per node
    MIN(j.campaign_id) OVER(PARTITION BY j.journey_id, j.node_id) AS first_message_id_in_node,
    node_order_number
  FROM google_sheets_marketing.lifecycle_journeys j
  LEFT JOIN node_order_number n ON n.journey_id = j.journey_id AND n.node_id = j.node_id
  WHERE lower(j.domain) = 'driver')

,combined_properties AS (

  SELECT
    'campaign' AS message_type,
    message_id,
    message_name,
    lower(CASE

    first_start_dt AS start_date,

Hi there, we haven't heard from you in a while. If you would like to keep this request open or if you have additional information, just reply.

I suppose what we want to achieve with this, is actioning on availability metrics in a manner that is most impactful - i.e. focusing on products where improving availability will have the most impact on sales. 

What we then want to take into account is:

# General “_size_” of the SKU (how much sales it could have generated).
# _Time_ dimension - was an SKU unavilable during a high-demand time or a low-demand time.

Typically the “holy grail” of calculating this is the “_lost sales_” approach - where we hindcast the demand for each SKU on an hourly level (or use the initial demand forecast; although this has downsides - i.e. if the demand forecast was correct, why is there an availability issue in the first place), and “backfill” how much sales we lost. And then tracking that, right next to Waste. Tracking those two becomes a next step in the “evolution” of an availability metric, making it expressed in terms of value, and can essentially replace tracking availability itself. But we can start with something simpler 🙂 

Achieving weighting availability by the _size_ dimension (i.e. unavailability of a popular SKU having a higher weight than availability of an unpopular SKU) is quite straightforward, and in its simplest form could be achieved through simply weighting by an SKU's total historical daily/weekly sales. We can assign a new name to this metric (e.g. _Sales-weighted Availability %_) and start measuring it together with general availability. I think we should not replace the original un-weighted availability metric, but keep tracking both, at least until we conclude otherwise. Perhaps it’s a more interpretable, and easier-to-implement approach than using MenuViews (which are also not product-specific). *Wdyt?*

Regarding weighting by the time dimension (i.e. unavailability of an SKU during high-demand hours having a higher weight than during low-demand hours) - that’s certainly a useful thing, and with this we are coming closer to having a “lost sales” metric, but:

# I’d suggest to leave it as Step 2. Current availability metric is already computationally complex and causes performance issues, and this one would explode it even more. 
# We’d need to analyse what indeed can be used as a good approximation of demand, and if MenuViewed per store would not bias the demand proxy for different categories (for products where intra-week and intra-day demand pattern differs from total store demand pattern; e.g. alcohol). 
# Perhaps most importantly - is it actionable? I’m not too familiar yet with the back-room process, but in case, for instance: (a) demand forecast is done on daily level and (b) deliveries are made only once a day, say in the morning and (c) acceptance is made right upon delivery. How could we action on intra-day-weighted availability metric better than we can action on a day-level availability metric? 

If we talk about _intra-week weighted availability_ as opposed to _intra-day weighted availability_ (i.e. _high-demand days having a bigger weight than low-demand days_, rather than _high-demand hours having a bigger weight than low-demand hours_), it makes it somewhat more sensible. But still, probably the biggest action here is around using product- and time-weights when evaluating and fine-tuning demand forecasting model (using demand-weighted error metrics), rather than using it for tracking day-to-day operations. *Please correct me if I’m missing something* 🙂

In the meanwhile, we can start with the Sales-weighted availability metric.

Hello team,

Any feedback on this ticket?

No, in the context of that call, the ask was to have a more precise metric of availability on the store level: we want to understand how our assortment looks like for a customer once a customer is really opening the app. Hence we don’t really care if they checked particular categories or items — so {{Menu Viewed}} is quite okay for that. 

Main concern is that week-level availability is measuring “average temperature per hospital”, so I would totally not deviate from the essence of the request.

Once we have demand-weighted availability, approximating sales-weighted availability is actually quite easy: it could be ballpark captured by calculating demand-weighted availability metric for specific parts of assortment:

* all
* anchor
* bananas, tomatos and milk
* fresh
* (other categories)
* …

Sure computationally challenging (I know), but why should it stop us? If you need more denormalized data (e. g., dump entire assortment every X minutes in every store) — you can always ask engineers for that. Or build ETLs. ¯\\_(ツ)_/¯ 

PS. With sales-weighted metric there’s yet another challenge: sales depend on availability, so this metric might self-improve — worse availability — worse sales — better sales-weighted availability.
tl;dr: we want to know if bananas are missing in the morning (low demand) or in the evening (high demand).

{quote}Perhaps most importantly - is it actionable? I’m not too familiar yet with the back-room process{quote}

Sure. Hypothesis is that availability correlates with conversion from menu viewed to checkout. So with a decent metric here we can:

* hopefully finally learn why we suck, where we suck, and at what time of the day we suck
* know which stores / cities / countries perform badly and dig deeper in their Supply Chain challenges

!image-20220613-075130.png|width=50%!

!image-20220613-075230.png|width=1218,height=689!

Hi\!

Of course, what happens here is the user is charged a fine but does not have enough money on his card - we cannot capture the charge so the system adds it to his Bolt Balance as debt. The user rents another scooter, now has enough money to pay for the previous order (the one with the fine) and to cover the preauth amount, ends the order, we capture both the payment for the 2nd order and the debt for the first one.

Now we can issue a refund in the first order, the one the user was fined for, that will add the refunded amount to his Bolt Balance. We can also issue a refund for the 2nd order, this will transfer the charged amount, the price of the 2nd order and the debt added to it, to the user’s payment method.

The agents do not know that the system works this way so they issue a refund in the 1st order and the user has the amount added to his Bolt Balance despite having been promised a refund to his payment method.

The system’s logic is quite strange in my opinion but I hope this clarifies the issue.

* User canceled from active order.

* If a ride finishes when app is inactive, upon reopening the app a new session gets created

The intellectual property clause says: 

_'In relation to Intellectual Property, the Sponsor  will leave IFEMA MADRID harmless with respect to any claim or claim by the holders of rights to works and services used in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement, undertaking to defend IFEMA MADRID from any legal requirement. received by IFEMA MADRID in relation to an unauthorized use of works and services protected by intellectual property rights. In any case, in the event that IFEMA MADRID is forced, by court order or by virtue of a request received by the respective owner of rights, to cease the use of the protected works and services, or is condemned by a final judgment for said use, the Sponsor undertakes to leave IFEMA MADRID harmless with respect to any pronouncement of condemnation to which this entity may be subject.'_ 

Normally we do not agree with this type of indemnity. I propose to make it mutual, substituting IFEMA for Parties as follows: 

_'In relation to Intellectual Property,_ *_the Parties_*  _will leave the other harmless with respect to any claim or claim by the holders of rights to works and services used in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement, undertaking to defend the other_ *_Party_* _from any legal requirement received by this Party in relation to an unauthorized use of works and services protected by intellectual property rights ...'_

Most of the data we need for the reports similar to BP reports, we have it already in our reseller schema.The following are missing:

* Invoice number
* Invoice URL (need UUID)
* Driver name
* Driver VAT code
* Distance
* Duration
* Price & VAT breakdown

All of this data can be found in the invoice. However, there doesn't seem to be a good way to fetch all invoices by reseller for us. Therefore we have two options:

h3. 1. Fetch from invoicing by Order + City IDs

There can be quite a few orders that we would need to fetch the data for. This query can also be quite time-consuming depending on the number of orders in the reporting period. Therefore, for this one, we will need to have an async flow. A good-to-have for this flow would be an API that takes a list of Order + City IDs and returns the invoices for them.

h3. 2. Store (& duplicate) invoice data on our end

We can store the required data on our end on the [invoice ready event|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/dfd5f35aa2f9ec1ff6e7c0253c067bd4bc4136d7/src/platform/commerce/invoicing_user/main/service/UserInvoiceGenerator.ts#L1038]. Since we’ll then have all the data in our DB, we can do JOINs and make this a synchronous flow. However, there are some issues with this approach including pushback from the team owning RH invoices. Some gotchas mentioned by the owning team include:

* regulatory requirements.
* invoice state can change including new states being introduced in the near future.
* keeping the data sources in sync.

Hey Andrew\! I did a quick scan of the Groundscope docs. If time, we can also cover this during the VenueButler call today, but overall it’s the same old - while object of the agreement is overall clear (the API integration/ co-operation) then every single player comes with their own unique approach, be it any of the early aggregators, Mobimeo, Groundscope etcetc. 

In each case all of these templates seek to offload the majority of obligations to the other party, while keeping most of the rights to itself. In this case e.g Bolt needs to take full liability for the drivers, acquire different insurance, to name just a few. Also a lot of nuance is different from our standard.

So how to go about it?

# Alt 1. Whenever realistic (i.e we have the upper hand in terms of bargaining position) we should push for our template. In our template we have taken a relatively balanced approach, we know it, hence we can move faster (and cheaper) with this. Also in practice it has proven to work fine. _We can already adjust our template before first sharing it to accommodate some needs of the counterparty, and explain the background why our template is a good fit._

Zendesk Clarification about overages:

The term in question is a standard term which has been designed in conjunction with Revenue recognition team and is part of the way overages would be recognised and feature in the variable contribution projections.  If detail is needed on the ins-and-outs of this, and why the language was drafted in the specific way it has been, then I can suggest a technical call would be required with our rev rec team. Unfortunately it can not be changed.
 
From my understanding of your concern is that Bolt would be billed the list price during the term rather than the $142.00.  I think a bit more clarification about how the invoicing would go will be helpful, so let me illustrate.
 
The way Zendesk recognises the revenue is on a straightforward linear basis.  So,  6000/12= 500 agent months per month.  (Bolt will of course have access to up to 6000 in every month of the subscription, that is a different issue to how the revenue gets recognised.)   So, let's take a scenario where we are in month 3 - Bolt should, notionally, have used 1500 in month 3, but let's assume you have actually used 2000. Bolt would be 'running hot'  and, even though there will not be any negative number in the tracker and the tracker would show 2000 used, 4000 left, the customer would be expected to 'true up'  by doing an agent adds of at least 500 and possibly more to meet the expected increase in consumption.  That 'true up'  would be charged at the price of 142.00 and only apply should you need it. In your example the numbers will be declining so true up may not be needed unless you are seeing more demands etc. Note, in this scenario the customer would not "have exceeded the number of Agent Seat months purchased" because they would not yet have exceeded the 6000 - but they would be heading in that direction, so they would be expected to do a 'true-up'  so that they don't end up exceeding it. In Bolt's case the opposite will be happening for the true up as you will be declining agents not increasing them so this should not be of concern. 
 
What would be the scenario in which Zendesk would charge list price?  Let's say a customer runs hot during the annual term and refuses to do any true-ups.  The year ends and at that point the tracker would be showing a negative amount.  This negative amount of agent months would be separately and retrospectively billed at List price (even if the subscription were to renew, they would still be billed as they would have been consumed fully in the current year).  This is the scenario  in which, as the language has it "the subscriber exceeds the number of Agent Seat Month purchased in the order form......prior to the subscription term end date". As this contract will be only 1 year in length again I do not envision this scenario to happen and you could add the agents as needed.

CASE WHEN payment_type = 'payment_problem' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS payment_problem, 
CASE WHEN payment_type = 'chargeback' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS chargeback,
CASE WHEN payment_type = 'refund finished' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS order_refunded,
CASE WHEN (payment_type = 'failed_payment' AND o.uncovered_amount IS NULL) OR (o.uncovered_amount IS NOT NULL AND o.uncovered_amount != 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS failed_payment,
CASE WHEN (chargeback=1 OR failed_payment=1 OR payment_problem=1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS bad_payment,
ROUND(CASE WHEN (failed_payment = 1 AND o.uncovered_amount IS NULL) THEN o.capture_amount WHEN (o.booking_id IS NOT NULL AND o.uncovered_amount > 0) THEN o.uncovered_amount ELSE 0 END,2) AS failed_payment_amount,
ROUND(CASE WHEN (failed_payment = 1 AND o.uncovered_amount IS NULL) THEN o.capture_amount/r.rate WHEN (o.booking_id IS NOT NULL AND o.uncovered_amount > 0) THEN o.uncovered_amount/r.rate ELSE 0 END,2) AS failed_payment_amount_eur
FROM public.company_order co 
JOIN public.company_order_try ot ON co.id = ot.order_id AND co.city_id = ot.city_id AND ot.state = 'finished' 
JOIN null_pred np ON np.search_tok = co.search_token AND np.city_id = co.city_id 
JOIN max_distance md ON md.order_id = co.id AND md.city_id = co.city_id  
LEFT JOIN commerce.orders o ON o.order_id = co.id AND o.city_id = co.city_id AND o.order_type = 'order'
LEFT JOIN public.currency_exchange_rates r ON DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE(co.created) AND r.currency = ot.price_currency 
LEFT JOIN public.ride_hailing_invoicing_order_pricing_transaction ptr ON ptr.order_id = co.id AND ptr.city_id = co.city_id 
LEFT JOIN public.ride_hailing_invoicing_tips_transaction_details tip ON tip.city_id = ptr.city_id AND tip.order_pricing_transaction_id = ptr.id 
LEFT JOIN pii.user_user u ON u.id = co.user_id 
WHERE co.created >= '2022-01-01'
AND co.dispatcher_id IS NULL
AND co.reseller_id IS NULL
AND co.company_id IS NULL
AND co.payment_method_type != 'default' 
AND co.payment_method_type != 'business'{code}

+*Dangerous goods*+  

Clause 3.4 says: _Contractor Personnel must have completed at the expense of the Contractor so called ADR 1.3 training as per Section 1.3. of the ADR. The Contractor must keep the documentation of the completed training and provide proof of completed training within one day upon Bolt’s request._

I have read section 1.3 of the ADR and it says: 

+*_1.3.1_*+ 

*_SCOPE AND APPLICABILITY_* 

_Persons employed by the participants referred to in Chapter 1.4, whose duties concern the carriage of dangerous goods, shall be trained in the requirements governing the carriage of such goods  appropriate to their responsibilities and duties. Employees shall be trained in accordance with 1.3.2 before assuming responsibilities and shall only perform functions, for which required training has not yet been provided, under the direct supervision of a trained person. Training requirements specific to security of dangerous goods in Chapter 1.10 shall also be addressed._ 

_NOTE 1: With regard to the training for the safety adviser, see 1.8.3 instead of this section._ 

_NOTE 2: With regard to the training of the vehicle crew, see Chapter 8.2 instead of this section._ 

_NOTE 3:  For training with regard to Class 7, see also 1.7.2.5._  

+*_1.3.2_*+ 

*_NATURE OF THE TRAINING_* 

_The training shall take the following form, appropriate to the responsibility and duties of the individual concerned._ 

+*_1.3.2.1_*+ 

*_GENERAL AWARENESS TRAINING_* 

_Personnel shall be familiar with the general requirements of the provisions for the carriage of dangerous goods._ 

+*_1.3.2.2_*+ 

*_FUNCTION-SPECIFIC TRAINING_* 

_Personnel shall be trained, commensurate directly with their duties and responsibilities in the requirements of the regulations concerning the carriage of dangerous goods._ 

_Where the carriage of dangerous goods involves a multimodal transport operation, the personnel shall be aware of the requirements concerning other transport modes._ 

+*_1.3.2.3_*+ 

*_SAFETY TRAINING_* 

_Commensurate with the degree of risk of injury or exposure arising from an incident involving the carriage of dangerous goods, including loading and unloading, personnel shall be trained in the hazards and dangers presented by dangerous goods._ 

_The training provided shall aim to make personnel aware of the safe handling and emergency response procedures._

+*_1.3.2.4_*+ 

_The training shall be periodically supplemented with refresher training to take account of changes in regulations._ 

+*_1.3.3_*+ 

*_DOCUMENTATION_* 

_Records of training received according to this Chapter shall be kept by the employer and made available to the employee or competent authority, upon request. Records shall be kept by the employer for a period of time established by the competent authority. Records of training shall be verified upon commencing a new employment_.

So together with [~accountid:622852fd6a4c4c0070b16e6d] we tried to understand the actionability of this metric, some of our thoughts:


* The basic SCM question is not “either to order goods to be delivered in the morning or in the evening” but “on Thursday or on Friday” (except ultra fresh). And for ultra-fresh the delivery should most likely take place in the morning always, before the store opening or right after it. Moreover, currently due to low volumes we cannot control the delivery schedules and just comply with whatever the supplier proposes.
* This means that weighting the availability would make sense on intra-week level (giving more weight to Fridays than to Mondays) as opposed to intra-day level. 
*  We also need to decide what to use as a weighting base (either views or orders): if “views” then we’re actually measuring the demand but we cannot split by categories, if “orders” then we can split by categories (in a way to make it actionable) but this would be not the pure demand.

Sounds to me we might have some problems here with future payouts.

Not in all cases the account the payout goes to will be belonging to the driver in question.

Here’s a breakdown of setups one might come across looking through Latvian driver profiles:

We have drivers that work with their own company and then _usually_ they get their payout to their own company account (account holder is their company) or their own personal account. In which case the driver has all rights of representation.

Then we have drivers that work with their own company and for whatever reason would like to have their payout to a different IBAN that doesn’t belong to them directly - brothers, cousins, mothers, fathers etc account.

Then we have fleet drivers that get their payouts to - fleets bank account, or their own personal bank account, or 3rd parties bank account (brother,sisters, mother etc)

So I fear there’s a lot of clarifying that might be headed our way if we will need to clarify such details as above (with screenshots etc), and whilst some entities might have similar names to entities that are in global sanctions list, I don’t understand then how are they (Citibank) not concerned about every payout made, as the end user (receiver) might be linked to sanctioned companies in different ways anyway (as a beneficiary or some other form), so technically all payouts are of concern in my opinion. User Retention

Cash-block status

* GE, NG, and ZA have low cash-block rate following early cashout usage. Only <3% of users are cash-blocked after 12 weeks since initial usage of early cashout
* KE, TZ, and GH have mid-to-high cash-block rate, around 6%, 12%, and 20% respectively after 12 weeks since initial usage of early cashout. However, we can't say that they're getting cash-blocked because of early cashout (need more analysis)

{code:sql}
select city_name,
date_trunc('week',event_ts) week_ts,
count(vehicle_id) swaps,
        avg(final_charge) avg_charge_of_battery_after_swap,
        count(case when final_charge<50 then vehicle_id else null end) count_swaps_with_swapping_battery_less_50,
        count(case when final_charge between 50 and 60 then vehicle_id else null end) count_swaps_with_swapping_battery_50_60,
        count(case when final_charge between 60 and 70 then vehicle_id else null end) count_swaps_with_swapping_battery_60_70,
        count(case when final_charge between 70 and 80 then vehicle_id else null end) count_swaps_with_swapping_battery_70_80,
        count(case when final_charge between 80 and 90 then vehicle_id else null end) count_swaps_with_swapping_battery_80_90,
        count(case when final_charge between 90 and 101 then vehicle_id else null end) count_swaps_with_swapping_battery_over_90
from 
(
 select 
 *,
 datediff('second', event_ts, lead(event_ts,1) over (partition by vehicle_id order by event_ts asc)) time_till_next_event,
 datediff('second', event_ts, lead(event_ts,2) over (partition by vehicle_id order by event_ts asc)) time_till_next_next_event,
 lead(type_of_action,1) over (partition by vehicle_id order by event_ts asc) next_type_of_action,
 lead(type_of_action,2) over (partition by vehicle_id order by event_ts asc) next_next_type_of_action,
 lead(charge,1) over (partition by vehicle_id order by event_ts asc) next_charge,
 lead(charge,2) over (partition by vehicle_id order by event_ts asc) next_next_charge,
 case when next_next_charge>next_charge then 1 else 0 end next_next_is_bigger,
 case 
 	when next_type_of_action='go_online' and next_next_type_of_action='go_online' and next_next_is_bigger=1 and time_till_next_next_event<600 then next_next_charge
 	when next_type_of_action='go_online' and next_next_is_bigger=0 and time_till_next_event<600 then next_charge
 end final_charge
 from (
SELECT
     be.created AS event_ts
    , b.vehicle_id
    , ct.id AS city_id
    , ct.name AS city_name
    , 'swap' as type_of_action
    , -1 as charge
    , external_type
    , external_id
FROM rental.rental_order_charger_action_change_battery_event be
join rental.rental_order_charger_action_change_battery b
on be.charger_action_change_battery_id = b.id and be.connection_id=b.connection_id
JOIN rental.rental_fleet_search_category sc on b.search_category_id=sc.id
JOIN public.admin_system_city ct on sc.city_id=ct.id
WHERE b.state ='battery_changed' and be.to_state = 'battery_changed'
and be.created >='2022-05-15'
union all 
select dateadd('second',120,e.created) AS event_ts,
vehicle_id,
   ct.id AS city_id,
    ct.name AS city_name,
   'go_online' as type_of_action,
   charge,
   external_type,
   external_id
from rental.rental_order_vehicle_state_event e
JOIN rental.rental_fleet_search_category sc on e.search_category_id=sc.id
JOIN public.admin_system_city ct on sc.city_id=ct.id
where e.created>='2022-05-15'
 and e.type = 'is_available_for_order' and e.value=1
)
order by vehicle_id asc, event_ts asc 
)
where type_of_action ='swap' and final_charge is not null
group by 1,2
order by 1 asc, 2 asc

Got my hands on a prelive version of the driver app & was able to look around what’s there. So let’s say we’re a driver & just received our monthly invoice for x amount. To confirm how much I paid commission there’s a few options: 

# Check the balance view/box on the invoice - there we have the balance before/after the period showing the payments & payouts. Relatively easily to eyeball the % invoiced amount vs total payments/orders

[^driver_invoice.pdf]

*2.* Check the monthly earnings from Driver App - in order to do so driver would have to:

a. open the app
b. click on today’s earnings
c. switch to a monthly view
d. make the way to the previous month where we see the earnings/expenses & net earnings (earnings - expenses)

But this doesn’t give very detailed overview but can be used to roughly see the total earnings & how much commission they’ve paid/need to pay

*3*. Check the weekly earnings from Driver Portal - for this the driver would have to:

a. open the app
b. click the settings -> account -> driver portal (which opens up a web browser)
c. menu -> balance report
d. pull a weekly balance report showing the weekly transactions fees & earnings etc

[^Bolt Saldo Kokkuvõte - 2022W13 (1) (1).pdf]

The level of detail on the report is sufficient as it gives a good aggregate overview of the transactions done during the week + gives a daily breakdown (which I assume is more than enough for a regular driver). The issue for the weekly report is that it’s weekly (as the payout is weekly) but the invoicing is monthly (meaning it’s difficult to compare the 2 documents without actually crunching numbers in excel). 

Now which comes to the possible areas for improvement: 

# Driver Portal (where all the good stuff is) for me (first time user) is hidden in the app. I would have no idea to search for it under settings → account. Maybe we could incorporate this a bit better (it’s own section under settings) OR
# regarding billing - all the reports, invoices etc are in the Portal (which I couldn’t find initially). Maybe we could put a link to invoices/reports directly on the Driver Earnings screen? If the app team complains about bad UI maybe we could allow this link only when the monthly breakdown of the earnings is selected etc? 
# the weekly reports - we see a lot of CS tickets asking for daily/monthly/yearly reporting (will have to figure out the impact in more detail [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/BA-1045|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/BA-1045|smart-link] ) but after discussing this with Maret for the drivers having the reports not locked in a specific timeframe but the driver could select the time period themselves would be a great solution. As we already have all the data there (daily breakdown) not sure how much effort it would be to remove the weekly limit & let the drivers choose their own timeframe (this week, last week, last month, this quarter, last year, custom etc)

_In case of companies employing_ *_between 50 and 249 employees_*_, the law imposes the appointment of dedicated OHS workers or the implementation of an internal dedicated OHS department. *_The dedicated OHS worker_* _can be appointed from the local company’s full-time employees and should handle the OHS activities as primary responsibilities and have other job attributions only on the side, to the extent the regular working hours allow such cumulus. _The law imposes several minimum professional requirements for dedicated OHS workers, such as high school degree with technical or math/science profile, as well as dedicated OHS training (at least the 80 hours basic module)._

*_The internal dedicated OHS department_* _should be organized as a stand-alone department within the organization, formed of the local company’s full-time employees hired to handle exclusively OHS responsibilities. _The OHS Committee should have the following structure:_

* _the company’s legal representative;_

# *What is the general position under Maltese law about free delivery from alcohol stores, both offline and online through platforms?*

_There is currently no legal framework to regulate the delivery from alcohol stores. Operators must adhere to regulations in relation to the sale of specific products, where the minimum purchasing age of alcohol is 17. If a vendor, manufactures, blends, or prepares alcoholic beverages, they must be in possession of the necessary licences._ 

*2. If no issues with regard to the above, how should we reflect this in our platform e.g. “free delivery provided by the store” disclaimer or similar?* 

_Given that presently there are no regulations as to the delivery of alcohol, you may wish to adopt free delivery services for goods. You may wish to add a disclaimer for the verification of age upon delivering any alcoholic beverages by means of valid identification (I.D.).  You may also wish to include a disclaimer similar to "drink responsibly" to promote consumption of alcoholic beverages in moderation._ 

*3. Any other requirements with regard to alcohol sale or “promotion" that should be taken into account (apart from age verification by the courier)?*

_In relation to the sale/promotion of alcohol, the marketing and advertising of alcohol is governed by the Subsidiary Legislation 350.24. It is important to note that adverts/teleshopping for alcohol shall not be addressed to individuals under the age of 18 or use treatments likely to be of particular appeal to them . Any offers that pertain to alcoholic beverages, such as a cut-off prices, buy two and get one free offers or similar forms of adverts must not encourage any form of excessive drinking. Together with these points, any sale of alcohol and its respective promotion must be done modestly as not to promote the over-drinking._

_Unfortunately no changes to the selling under purchase price regulations so far (i.e., Government Ordinance no. 99/2000 on retail products and services), although draft legislation in this respect has been discussed and also the Romanian competition authority advised that such rules are not necessary for non-dominant companies._

_As regards practicalities, sanctions are imposed by the National Consumer Protection Association (ANPC) and summaries of the findings are generally made public from time to time._

_Just to provide some statistical information, usually about 50% of the companies which are under control have some irregularities in organizing promotions and the average fine is around 3.000 lei (approx. 600 EUR). During the last years the controls have been more focused on Black Friday campaigns and the practice of online retailers of spiking the retail price a few days before announcing the discounts (whereas the legal obligation is for the benchmark price to constitute an average of the previous 30 days). This, of course, is not related to selling under acquisition cost, however all promotions and discounts are verified simultaneously and this is the one type of promotion which has particularly stood out recently._

_Another aspect which may be of interest is that the prohibition on selling retail under acquisition cost derives from rules regulating unfair competition, the rationale being that such practice is likely to unfairly harm competitors, and it may even harm the whole market. The CJEU held in the Judgment of October 19, 2017, Rec.C-295/16, that the Directive 2005/29/EC on unfair commercial practices must be interpreted as opposing a national provision containing a general prohibition of offering or making sales below cost and establishing exceptions to said prohibition based on criteria that do not appear in the Directive itself. While this decision did not trigger any change in Romanian legislation, it may be construed that, since the sale below cost is not among the practices provided for in Annex I to the Directive 2005/29/EC, the imposition of a sanction may only apply only if the sale below cost can be described as “unfair”, based on the the criteria provided in Art. 5 of the same directive (Euronics Belgium, C‑343/12, EU:C:2013:154, paragraph 25). Furthermore, the CJEU also held that, given that selling at a loss is not included among the practices referred to in Annex I to  the Directive 2005/29/EC, the imposition of a penalty for infringement of the prohibition of such selling at a loss must be preceded by an analysis, undertaken having regard to the facts of each particular case, of whether that selling is ‘unfair’ in the light of the criteria set out in Articles 5 of Directive 2005/29/EC, and cannot be based on a presumption which the trader is required to rebut (Judgment of the CJEU of October 19, 2017, Rec.C-295/16, para. 42)._

_However, this may be an argument which is more likely to be successful in court than before the administrative authorities applying fines, as the current Romanian legislation does not allow them any liberty in appreciating whether the practice was unfair and, in practice, the administrative authorities do not make such distinction._

_Finally, one other aspect to be considered is that Government Ordinance no. 99/2000 on retail products and services allows premium sales, where the customer is provided free of charge identical products and services with the ones acquired or free samples. If the promotion would consist of a one-off giveaway, then this option could have better chances of being defended as escaping the provisions of Government Ordinance no. 99/2000._ 

_Also, point 437 of Ministry of Finance Order 1802/2014 on the annual financial statements allows for the awarding of promotional points (e.g. vouchers) which may be used to acquire goods or services freely or at a discounted price. Since this is regulated separately from promotions under Government Ordinance no. 99/2000 on retail products and services, this option could also have better chances of being defended as escaping the provisions of Government Ordinance no. 99/2000._

{code:sql}SELECT /* ROUTE READONLY=1 */
  p.created, p.state, pmu.payment_user_id, p.id AS payment_id, o.app_version, o.type, o.business_line, pending_pr.amount, p.currency, o.city_id, pmu.payment_method_id AS token, pmu.card_bin, pmu.card_alias AS card_fingerprint, pending_pr.token AS invoice_id, pending_pr.token_data AS transaction_id
FROM payment AS p
JOIN payment_row pending_pr ON p.id = pending_pr.payment_id AND pending_pr.type = 'prepare' AND (pending_pr.state = 'pending' OR pending_pr.state = 'error')
LEFT JOIN payment_row other_r ON p.id = other_r.payment_id AND (other_r.type != 'prepare' OR other_r.state != 'pending' AND other_r.state != 'error')
LEFT JOIN payment_order o ON p.payment_order_id = o.id
LEFT JOIN payment_method_user pmu ON p.payment_method_type = pmu.payment_method_type AND p.payment_method_id = pmu.payment_method_id AND pmu.payment_user_id = o.payment_user_id
WHERE p.state  = 'created' AND
      p.payment_method_type = 'processout' AND
      pending_pr.type = 'prepare' AND
      pending_pr.state = 'pending' AND
      p.created > DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 24 HOUR)
GROUP BY p.id, o.id, pmu.id, pending_pr.id
HAVING COUNT(other_r.id) = 0;{code}

Script for querying delays



{code:sql}select 
	model, 
	city_name, 
	count(time_diff), 
	avg(time_diff) avg_from_expected_till_actual,
	count(case when time_diff>=3 then time_diff else null end) sec_3_and_more,
	count(case when time_diff>=10 then time_diff else null end) sec_10_and_more,
	count(case when time_diff>=30 then time_diff else null end) sec_30_and_more,
	count(case when time_diff>=60 then time_diff else null end) sec_60_and_more,
	count(case when time_diff>=120 then time_diff else null end) sec_120_and_more
from 
(
select v.model, c.name as city_name, e.type, e.value,
datediff('second',e.created,lead(e.created) over (partition by e.vehicle_id order by e.created asc)) time_diff,
order_id,
lead(e.order_id) over (partition by e.vehicle_id order by e.created asc) next_order_id,
lead(e.type) over (partition by e.vehicle_id order by e.created asc) next_type,
lead(e.value) over (partition by e.vehicle_id order by e.created asc) next_value
from rental.rental_order_vehicle_state_event e 
join rental.rental_fleet_vehicle v on e.vehicle_id = v.id
join rental.rental_fleet_search_category sc on e.search_category_id =sc.id
join admin_system_city c on sc.city_id  = c.id
where e.type in ('expected_is_started', 'actual_is_started')
and e.created >'2022-06-01'
order by vehicle_id asc, e.created asc
)
where type = 'expected_is_started' and value=1 and next_type='actual_is_started' and next_value=1 and order_id=next_order_id
group by 1,2
order by 1 asc, 2 asc{code}

TL/DR: this issue most probably will be gone once we roll-out migration to new signup/login API - [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/CLIENTAPP-15199|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/CLIENTAPP-15199|smart-link]. But that would need to be double-checked, of course.

Context:
The problem is caused by the fact that polling of {{/getVehicles}} endpoint could be setup in two modes - when parallel orders feature is disabled, and when it is enabled. And, unfortunately, it was implemented in a way that this poller is started just before app is switched to "Logged in" state. For case when user logs into the app the poller is initially configured as parallel orders feature is disabled, and after app proceeds to “Logged in” state, this poller is already started, and it is not reconfigured with new value for feature-flag. For cases when app starts with already logged in user there is no such a problem, as location config we are getting from {{/getAppStateOnStartup}} endpoint has our feature-flag set correctly before app is switched to “Logged in” state, and so we are configuring the poller correctly from the very start.

In [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/CLIENTAPP-15199|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/CLIENTAPP-15199|smart-link] we are supplementing all the endpoints finishing the login/signup flows with updated location config, so the value we are using for poller configuration should be up to date, when app transitions to “Logged in” state.
